adversarial_audit.objection: The finite reciprocal screen already proved the 1/d law.
adversarial_audit.resolution: It did not. The screen measured values; this module derives the operator, its multiplicities, and the exact conditions under which a value can be one.

adversarial_audit.objection: Every star correlation is a single reciprocal irrep dimension.
adversarial_audit.resolution: False in general. The exact value is a product of two carrier reciprocals; finite controls only ever realized a one-dimensional second carrier because their membership blocks are singletons.

adversarial_audit.objection: The 1/(n-1) bound makes the hierarchy well conditioned.
adversarial_audit.resolution: No. A leaf can meet exponentially many pair cores and the accumulated weighted degree is unbounded by this theorem.

adversarial_audit.objection: The theorem needs the collision-free sector.
adversarial_audit.resolution: It does not. Repeated-source controls outside the collision-free sector satisfy the same closed form.

adversarial_audit.objection: The disjoint waist bound is an equality.
adversarial_audit.resolution: It is exact on every screened control but only proved as an upper bound; a grid with genuine Kronecker multiplicity could be strictly smaller.

claim_gate.reason: The pair-core overlap operator is now exact and uniformly contracting off the common ranges, but nothing here controls how many such blocks meet one leaf or compiles the recoupling basis.

falsifiers_triggered: The conjectured single-reciprocal law is false in general; the exact value is a two-carrier product, so finite reciprocal spectra were an artifact of singleton membership blocks.
No nontrivial multiplicity-space 6j block exists for shared-vertex pair cores, so a Racah transform cannot be the obstruction at that level.
A uniformly small per-block correlation does not certify the hierarchy; the surviving falsifier is a carrier sector whose weighted degree reaches two.

proof_obligations.resolution: The closed form reproduces every dense ambient singular value, including rank and multiplicity, on all selected and screened controls.
Proved: off-common requires a nontrivial carrier, whose dimension is at least n-1, and self-conjugate channel collisions are dominated for n>=5.
The shared-vertex block is scalar. Genuine Kronecker multiplicity only enters when the two pair cores are vertex disjoint, where the waist bound replaces the scalar law.
Only an upper bound is proved. It is exact on every screened control, but the grid contraction has genuine 3j content and no closed form is derived.
Exact per-block weights do not bound a sum over many adjacent pair cores; the weighted-degree gate is untouched by this module.

summary: Derived and validated the exact shared-vertex pair-core overlap operator: 168 screened controls and 3 selected controls reproduce the closed form with maximum residual 5.829e-16. Proved the all-n off-common bound 1/(n-1) and a waist bound for vertex-disjoint cores that is exact on 40 of 40 controls. The weighted-degree accumulation gate is unchanged.

theorem_contract.carrier_grading: Both pair cores are graded by every membership-block isotypic label, so the overlap operator is block diagonal in that grading with no ambient computation.
theorem_contract.degenerate_racah_block: Two pairings of four self-dual carriers into invariants contract to the scalar 1/d; no nontrivial 6j mixing acts on multiplicity space for a shared-vertex star.
theorem_contract.disjoint_waist_bound: Vertex-disjoint pair cores sit inside products of commuting one-dimensional isotype projectors; any single row/column waist bounds the product norm, and the minimum waist is reported with its witness.
theorem_contract.exact_multiplicity: m_a(beta) m_ab(beta^d') m_ac(beta^d) m_abc(beta^{d xor d'}) * d_p m_b(p) m_bc(p^d) m_c(p^{d xor d'}) * dim T_empty.
theorem_contract.off_common_bound: A correlation is one exactly when both carriers are one dimensional; two isotype channels share a sector only when both carriers are self-conjugate, hence of dimension at least n-1. For n>=5 every off-common star correlation is at most 1/(n-1).
theorem_contract.scope: This governs one overlap block at a time. It does not bound the weighted degree of a leaf that meets many pair cores, and it is not an algorithmic statement.
theorem_contract.star_factorization: For a shared orientation the overlap is a direct sum of (1/(d_beta d_p)) times partial isometries, with cluster-one carrier beta on the patterns containing the shared orientation and cluster-two carrier p on the remaining nonempty patterns.
